newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNICEF pulls out of Brazzaville after shelling.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF pulls out of Brazzaville after shelling.

text.p: The U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF), which had been the last international relief agency operating in Brazzaville, Congo, said on Friday it had pulled out of the city due to heavy shelling.
UNICEF, which had been providing vaccinations and medical kits for about 100,000 children around Brazzaville, also said it feared its warehouse of supplies worth $200,000 would be looted.
The agency expressed concern that children were living in poor sanitary conditions amid a measles outbreak compounded by cases of malnutrition.

"We are very concerned that for the first time since the war started UNICEF has had to cease operations in the city," spokesman Hans Olsen told a news briefing in Geneva. "The situation is precarious, especially for children."
"Because of shelling, UNICEF has had to stop its operations in Brazzaville," he added, after speaking by telephone with UNICEF representative Eric Laroche now evacuated to Kinshasa.
Fighting broke out on June 5 after President Pascal Lissouba sent troops to surround the home of his predecessor, Denis Sassou Nguesso, as part of a crackdown on private militias.
Hundreds of people died, many of them civilians killed by indiscriminate shelling, before a fragile ceasefire was signed in July.
